rows.why_long: PrizePicks higher 1.5 needs 57% per pick for your entry; fair view 73% (fanduel 2.5, moved to this line). Averaging 1.8 over the last 8 games, higher than 1.5 in 65% of them (raw 55%, shrunk 70%). Projects 1.7 (raw 51%, shrunk 69%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 1.5 on PrizePicks. Each pick has to win 57% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 2.5, moved to this line) is 73%.
Game log, most recent first: 1, 2, 2, 4, 2, 2, 1, 0. Weighted average 1.8; went higher than 1.5 in 5 of 8 games (65% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.0, so the line is 0.3 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -5% on his average.
PFF: DEN plays man on 27% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 27%); he gains 0.89 yds/route vs man and 0.88 vs zone → +0% from scheme.
PFF: DEN allows 1.12 yds/route to RBs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.19) → -7% against his usual opponents.
PFF: He lines up in the slot 85% of the time; DEN's slot defenders allow 1.50 yds per coverage snap (league 1.54, tighter).
PFF: ARI's run blocking vs DEN's run defense: 0.7 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 1.1, league 1.2); he adds 2.9 after contact → -9% per carry.
Projection: we expect 1.7 catches on average — 0.2 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 55% and the matchup 51%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 70%, matchup 69%.
Bottom line: we give it 69% to win and it needs 57%. The edge is the difference: +12.1 points; that works out to about +21¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
